Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated `/_framework/debug` endpoint used by `dotnet watch`. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 | 8.0.32 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 | 9.0.21 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-96230](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-96230) ### Acknowledgements - Kevin Gosse ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.

The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy evaluates debugger expressions by generating and compiling C# source. Certain values originating in the application being debugged, including `ToString()` results, descriptions, and class names, are embedded in that generated source without consistent escaping. An attacker-controlled value can escape the generated string literal and execute code on a developer's machine when the developer evaluates an expression during debugging. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69791 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2.26478.115 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? You are affected if you use a vulnerable version of `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` to debug a Blazor WebAssembly application and evaluate an expression involving attacker-controlled application data. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. Install the latest supported version of .NET. 2. Update `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server` to the patched version for the .NET release used by the application. Once the updated package or runtime is installed, restart the debugger and development environment. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repositories are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime and https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repository (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Allow Go To Def from a file path in Razor in more places
Issues.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/84945 ish

Razor already supported Go To Def for file paths in C# string literals, and so I suggested in the compiler PR for asset paths (`~/` paths in Razor) that we should extend it to those as well. We thought that would be help up on requiring source mapping etc. so that issue was logged as a follow up.

This feature doesn't use source mappings, it just handles the `~/` directly in tooling, since that is already valid in MVC files, without asset path stuff, and isn't that complicated. This also expands the Go To Def to allow navigating to any file type, not just Razor files, which was an odd limitation. In fact if we left the limitation in place, it would have meant #84945 would have made no sense, and wouldn't have been possible to fix anyway.

Issues.Title: Fix missing documentation warnings with inheritdoc
Issues.Body:
When a member documents only its new parameters alongside `<inheritdoc>`, CS1573 and CS1712 currently ignore the documentation inherited from the referenced member. This change resolves inherited `<param>` and `<typeparam>` tags, including explicit `cref`, nested inheritance, XPath paths, overrides, and interface implementations, before reporting missing-tag warnings. A warning is still reported when the inherited documentation does not contain the matching tag.

Regression tests cover inherited parameter and type-parameter tags, inheritance chains, override/interface inheritance, and unmatched tags. The C# compiler build and focused documentation-comment tests passed on net10.0 and net472; formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

Issues.Title: Simplify RunTests Windows process discovery and log dump stages
Issues.Body:
Local timeout dump collection can itself hang while WMI enumerates processes, preventing both dump capture and test-process cleanup. The existing console output also makes it difficult to identify which collection stage stopped progressing.

Replace the Windows WMI query with one process-only Tool Help snapshot, enumerating PID/parent-PID pairs with `Process32FirstW` and `Process32NextW`. Reuse `SafeFileHandle` for snapshot disposal and remove RunTests' unused `System.Management` dependency. Existing descendant traversal, PID/start-time checks, Unix enumeration, and dump behavior remain unchanged.

Add same-line stage markers for child discovery and each dump attempt, followed by `completed` or `failed`:

```text
Getting child process tree for process dotnet (42) ... completed
Dumping process testhost (43) ... completed
```

A stalled operation leaves its start marker without a terminal status. Existing warning details, dump paths, and partial-file cleanup are preserved. Concurrent work items can still interleave console output.

### Validation

- Formatted the changed C# files and passed `git diff --check`.
- `dotnet build src\Tools\RunTests\RunTests.csproj -p:RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true --verbosity minimal` passed with zero warnings or errors, including after removing the explicit console flush calls.
- Temporary Windows smoke checks against the built assembly verified child/grandchild discovery, unrelated/root exclusion, leaf behavior, process exit, and native struct layout. Across 200 snapshots, the process handle count remained unchanged.
- Initial logging smoke checks verified discovery success/failure, a real dump's pending start and subsequent successful publication, and dump failure/cleanup. Temporary scripts and dumps were removed; no test projects were added.

The environmental WMI hang was not reproduced locally, so deterministic before/after regression efficacy for that hang remains unverified.

Issues.Title: Fix IDE0330 not reported when type contains multi-declarator fields
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86076

### Description

In CSharpUseSystemThreadingLockDiagnosticAnalyzer, when inspecting members of a type to find candidates for IDE0330, encountering a field with multiple declarators caused AnalyzeNamedType to return early.

Because the loop iterates over all members of the type, returning early aborted analysis for the rest of the type. Any valid single-declarator lock fields that followed were never analyzed, and no diagnostics were reported.

This change:
1. Replaces return with continue in CSharpUseSystemThreadingLockDiagnosticAnalyzer.AnalyzeNamedType so the remaining members of the type are still inspected.
2. Fixes the equivalence key in CSharpUseSystemThreadingLockCodeFixProvider which was set to Use_primary_constructor.
3. Adds unit tests covering types with multi-declarator fields both before and after valid lock fields, as well as multi-declarator private fields themselves.

Issues.Title: Exception in "Convert to regular constructor" on union type
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: VS Code 1.142.0 with C# DevKit preview 11.5.46, .NET SDK 11.0 RC 2.
> Compiler version: '5.13.0-1.26507.4 (13b4f255bdb00b9ef629b08d7be58db1650bdbb9)'. Language version: preview. Compiler path: 'c:\Users\user\.vscode\extensions\ms-dotnettools.csharp-11.3.18-win32-x64\.roslyn\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.dll'.

**Steps to Reproduce**:
```csharp
union U(string);
```
Open the lightbulb menu and select "Convert to regular constructor".

**Expected Behavior**: Either the action is performed, or the refactoring is not offered if it is not possible to perforn it.

**Actual Behavior**:
```
2026-10-15 08:49:28.658 [error] [codeAction/resolve]  System.InvalidOperationException: Operation is not valid due to the current state of the object.

   at Roslyn.Utilities.EnumerableExtensions.SelectAsArray[TSource,TResult](IReadOnlyCollection`1 source, Func`2 selector) in /_/src/Dependencies/Collections/Extensions/IEnumerableExtensions.cs:line 468

   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeActions.CodeAction.ComputeOperationsAsync(IProgress`1 progress, CancellationToken cancellationToken) in /_/src/Workspaces/Core/Portable/CodeActions/CodeAction.cs:line 310
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeActions.CodeAction.GetOperationsCoreAsync(Solution originalSolution, IProgress`1 progress, CancellationToken cancellationToken) in /_/src/Workspaces/Core/Portable/CodeActions/CodeAction.cs:line 247
   at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.Handler.CodeActionResolveHandler.HandleRequestAsync(CodeAction codeAction, RequestContext context, CancellationToken cancellationToken) in /_/src/LanguageServer/Protocol/Handler/CodeActions/CodeActionResolveHandler.cs:line 89
   at Microsoft.CommonLanguageServerProtocol.Framework.QueueItem`1.StartRequestAsync[TRequest,TResponse](TRequest request, TRequestContext context, IMethodHandler handler, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
2026-10-15 08:49:28.662 [error] Request codeAction/resolve failed.
  Message: Operation is not valid due to the current state of the object.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Make optimized Native AOT publish opt-in
Issues.Body:
🤖 Disable the default rollout of optimized Native AOT publish in .NET 11 while compatibility issues are addressed.

## Changes
- Default `UseOptimizedPublish` to `false` for Native AOT publish, restoring full `Build` execution and build hooks unless explicitly opted in.
- Retain `UseOptimizedPublish=true` opt-in, the non-AOT guard, and `NoBuild` behavior.
- Cover unset, explicit false, and explicit true values with and without `NoBuild`; assert build hooks, managed build outputs, and runnable native publish output. Keep the optimized project-reference test explicitly opted in.
- Update the optimization documentation to describe the .NET 11 opt-in behavior.

This is an independent change based on `release/11.0.1xx`, not stacked on #56650. It does not change `main`, schedule .NET 12 activation, or incorporate #56620, #56649, or #56650.

Related customer reports: #56618 and #56645. This defers the default rollout rather than replacing the fixes needed for explicit opt-in.

## Validation
- Built a fresh isolated Debug redist SDK with `build.cmd -skipCrossgen -skipInstallers`.
- Targeted `Microsoft.NET.Publish.Tests`: 9 passed, including all six default/false/true × build/no-build cases, optimized project references, unsupported publish modes, and the CoreBuild target-chain guard.
- Configured ILLink scope: `TrimmingOptions_are_defaulted_correctly_on_trimmed_apps`, 7 passed.
- Targeted runs retained TRX results and build binlogs under `artifacts/log/targeted-tests/`.

Validation was on Windows x64; the full test suite was not run. The redist build succeeded with existing unrelated NU1902/NU1903 warnings for `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` 8.0.1 in ApiCompat projects; focused test builds had no warnings.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Fix dotnet test relative project paths
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Port #56287 unchanged to `release/11.0.1xx`.

The command-wide `MSBuildSession` keeps its in-process node alive across target requests. For a multi-targeted test project, the first `ComputeRunArguments` request can leave the process working directory at the project directory. Evaluating the next framework then resolves the original relative project path from that directory and duplicates its directory segments.

Restore the caller's working directory after each MSBuild request in `finally`, while preserving the shared build session, result-cache behavior, and coherent binary log. Include the original regression coverage for positional and `--project` relative paths. Both changed files are byte-for-byte identical to the corresponding files in the original fix commit, `998c1cf9af8a1c689fc51a17f8dcd4b748f58375`.

Fixes #56196.

## Why this port

The original PR targeted `release/11.0.1xx-rc1`. Released SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105` does not contain the working-directory restoration and still reproduces the exception with both relative-path forms, including `Release --no-build --no-restore`. The same commands pass against the SDK built from this release branch with the port.

## Validation

Local Windows x64 validation, using release base `7b1bc9de0bfc2720ec47769249724f8084cd128c` plus this patch:

- Full SDK build: exit `0`.
- Focused regression, multi-targeting, binary-log, and device-selection coverage: **55/55 passed**, including both new relative-path data rows; exit `0`.
- Public reproduction: all five command variants below passed **4/4 tests** across `net10.0` and `net11.0`; each parent command exited `0`.

Build and focused-test commands (only the binary-log destination is shortened):

```powershell
.\build.cmd /bl:release-build.binlog /v:minimal

.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .github\skills\targeted-test\scripts\RunTargetedTests.cs -- `
  --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj `
  --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestBuildsAndRunsTestsForMultipleTFMs|FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestProducesBinaryLog|FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice"
```

The composed product was the complete `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet` layout, not just a separately built test assembly. The layout's `dotnet.dll` hash matched the compiled production CLI output.

| Component | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Built SDK | `11.0.100-dev` |
| MSBuild | `18.12.0-1.26473.115` |
| Test runtimes | `10.0.13`, `11.0.0-rtm.26473.115` |
| Reproduction xUnit | `4.0.2` |
| Reproduction Microsoft.Testing.Platform | `2.5.1` |

### Public reproduction

Used [jonsagara/DotnetTestBrokenReproduction](https://github.com/jonsagara/DotnetTestBrokenReproduction), branch `feature/net11rc2`, commit `2152c9f8741b0c2a8bc0f3268bb63d1c84f0ed2d`. Only the copied reproduction's `global.json` SDK version was changed to `11.0.100-dev` to select the built SDK; project sources, target frameworks, and packages were unchanged.

From the reproduction root, `$dotnet` is the absolute path to the built layout's `dotnet.exe`, `$project` is the absolute test-project path, and `$logs` is the diagnostics directory. Invocations used `DOTNET_ROOT`, `DOTNET_ROOT_X64`, and process `PATH` pointing to the built layout, `DOTNET_MULTILEVEL_LOOKUP=0`, `DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=0`, and an isolated `DOTNET_CLI_HOME`:

```powershell
& $dotnet test --project $project --configuration Release --report-xunit-trx `
  --results-directory "$logs\results" --results-directory-layout per-module `
  "-bl:$logs\absolute-release-control.binlog"
& $dotnet test src\AwesomeLibrary.Tests\AwesomeLibrary.Tests.csproj "-bl:$logs\positional-relative.binlog"
& $dotnet test --project src\AwesomeLibrary.Tests\AwesomeLibrary.Tests.csproj "-bl:$logs\explicit-relative.binlog"
& $dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build --no-restore `
  --project .\src\AwesomeLibrary.Tests\AwesomeLibrary.Tests.csproj "-bl:$logs\reported-release-no-build.binlog"
& $dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build --no-restore `
  --project $project "-bl:$logs\absolute-release-no-build.binlog"
```

Every invocation reported `total: 4`, `succeeded: 4`, and `failed: 0`, with no duplicated-path exception.

### Retained evidence and limits

The focused run produced `artifacts\log\targeted-tests\dotnet.Tests\20261015-134935-156328\test-results.trx` and `build.binlog`. Its TRX counters are total `55`, passed `55`, failed `0`, skipped `0`. The public reproduction produced a separate command binlog for every variant and two per-framework TRX reports for the absolute-path control, each with `2/2` passed.

The full build and reproduction logs, binary logs, component identities, and structured result summaries are retained in session artifacts under `issue-56196\release-validation`. These are local validation results, not a claim that a new SDK has shipped or that cross-platform CI has completed.

The full build also emitted eight existing `NU1902`/`NU1903` warnings for `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` in ApiCompat/PackageValidation dependencies; this port does not change or suppress those dependencies.

Issues.Title: Identify failing target framework in dotnet test device-selection errors
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Improve `dotnet test` device-selection failures to identify the project and target framework that failed, while preserving the selector's original error. Do not change device selection or normal all-target-framework execution.

For example:

```text
No devices are available for this project.
Device selection failed for project 'MauiTestRc2.csproj' (target framework 'net11.0-ios').
```

Projects without a target framework receive a project-only diagnostic. Includes regression coverage, regenerated localization, and clarification of multi-target device behavior in the existing MAUI run/test specification.

## Problem

`SelectDeviceForTfm` reported every failed device selection as a multiple-devices error, even when no devices were available. In a project targeting Android, iOS, and Mac Catalyst, selecting an Android device could succeed and then device selection for iOS could fail. The resulting error incorrectly suggested the Android device selection was still ambiguous and did not identify the failing framework.

This was reproduced interactively with .NET 11 RC 2 on Windows: selecting Pixel 5 among four connected Android devices succeeded, then iOS discovery returned no devices because `IsMacEnabled` was false. Android-only execution, including plain `dotnet test` on a project with only the Android entry in `TargetFrameworks`, succeeded.

## Validation

- Built the SDK and rebuilt/deployed the modified CLI into the isolated redist SDK.
- Verified four regression cases failed before the diagnostic fix.
- Ran `GivenDotnetTestSelectsDevice` and `GivenDotnetRunSelectsDevice` through `scripts/RunTests.cs`: **65 passed, zero skipped** after the final changes.
- Covered failures for explicit, first, and later target frameworks; preserved the original reason; checked that multiple-device diagnostics are not duplicated; covered projects without a target framework.
- Reviewed with Gemini 4 Argon and addressed its targetless-project diagnostic finding.

Single commit: `8ff360776c`.

Issues.Title: Enable SDK test scenario binlogs
Issues.Body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

The focused runner's `build.binlog` captures compilation of the test project, not necessarily the product build performed inside the test. When that scenario build does not request a binlog, an agent may need to edit the test code or reconstruct the build outside the test harness to enable capture. Diagnostic capture should be configurable for a test run rather than require a test-source change.

The [runner build](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/54bdffb71caf1f2b6aec2417e105f361f1137cbd/scripts/RunTests.cs#L321-L348) adds its binlog explicitly. [DotnetBuildCommand](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/54bdffb71caf1f2b6aec2417e105f361f1137cbd/test/Microsoft.NET.TestFramework/Commands/DotnetBuildCommand.cs#L11-L28) does not; [this existing build test](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/54bdffb71caf1f2b6aec2417e105f361f1137cbd/test/dotnet.Tests/CommandTests/Build/GivenDotnetBuildBuildsCsproj.cs#L18-L39) does not request one. Helix [uploads already-created binlogs](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/54bdffb71caf1f2b6aec2417e105f361f1137cbd/test/Microsoft.NET.TestFramework/Commands/TestCommand.cs#L271-L299); it does not create missing logs.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Provide an explicit diagnostic mode in the shared test harness, exposed through the local workflow, that captures known build-command wrappers without changing each test. Start with `MSBuildCommand` and `DotnetBuildCommand`; reuse [AspNetSdkTest's capture pattern](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/54bdffb71caf1f2b6aec2417e105f361f1137cbd/test/Microsoft.NET.TestFramework.MSTest/AspNetSdkTest.cs#L136-L170) and existing collection support.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The same fixture using `DotnetBuildCommand` without an authored `/bl` can run with capture disabled or enabled through a run setting, without test-source changes. Enabled capture produces readable scenario binlogs for successful and failing builds.
- Multiple commands, concurrent tests, and retry attempts retain distinct logs and a correlation entry in test output or attachments; no attempt overwrites another.
- An explicitly requested logger destination is respected and remains discoverable.
- Disabled mode preserves existing command/output behavior; individual commands can opt out when instrumentation would invalidate an argument/output test.
- Local retention and Helix collection work without searching unrelated directories or copying stale logs from previous runs.
- Fixtures verify both managed CLI and supported full-framework MSBuild launch paths, explicit logging, opt-out, retry uniqueness, and concurrent execution.

### Alternatives you've considered

Continue adding `BinLogArgument` per test or manually reconstruct the scenario build outside the harness. [#54863](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/54863) is a concrete example of changing test code to enable capture. Capturing every arbitrary command or globally enabling verbose output would be unnecessary and potentially disruptive.

### Additional context

Proposed priority: **P1**. Confidence: **high, 9/10**, source audit.
Proposed owner: SDK test-infrastructure maintainers, to confirm.
Related: [epic #55185](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/55185), [completed per-test repair #54863](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/54863), [noise reduction #54782](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/54782).
Non-goals: changing logging defaults for all tests, repairing a specific product failure, or implementing another binlog analyzer. Logs stay local/within existing CI retention; no automatic public uploads.

Issues.Title: [11.0 RC2 regression] NativeAOT publish fails with MSB3030 when XML documentation generation is enabled
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

Publishing a minimal NativeAOT console app targeting `net10.0` fails with .NET SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105` when `GenerateDocumentationFile` is enabled.

The same project publishes successfully using SDK `11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128`. The project has no explicit package references or custom build targets.

### Steps to reproduce

Create the following files in a new directory outside any other repository.

`AotXmlRepro.csproj`:

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>Exe</OutputType>
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <PublishAot>true</PublishAot>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

`Program.cs`:

```csharp
System.Console.WriteLine("Hello from NativeAOT.");
```

`global.json`:

```json
{
  "sdk": {
    "version": "11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105",
    "rollForward": "disable",
    "allowPrerelease": true
  }
}
```

On Windows x64 with the NativeAOT C++ build prerequisites installed, run:

```powershell
dotnet publish .\AotXmlRepro.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 -o .\publish -bl:rc2.binlog
```

### Expected behavior

Publishing succeeds, including copying the XML documentation file, as it does with .NET 11 RC1.

### Actual behavior

Native compilation completes, but publishing exits with code 1:

```text
Microsoft.NET.Publish.targets(396,5): error MSB3030:
Could not copy the file "bin\Release\net10.0\win-x64\AotXmlRepro.xml"
because it was not found.
```

After failure, `AotXmlRepro.xml` exists under `obj\Release\net10.0\win-x64`, but not under `bin\Release\net10.0\win-x64`, where publishing expects it.

### Is this a regression?

Yes. Changing only the SDK version in `global.json`, with clean output directories for each run:

- `11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128`: publishing succeeds and the native executable runs.
- `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`: publishing fails with MSB3030.

### Are there any workarounds?

Disabling publishing of the app's XML documentation avoids the failure:

```powershell
dotnet publish .\AotXmlRepro.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 -o .\publish -p:PublishDocumentationFile=false
```

Verified with a clean RC2 publish: publishing succeeds and the native executable runs. XML documentation generation remains enabled.

Issues.Title: .NET 11 RC2 regression: Web SDK app referencing a Web SDK library fails in Debug: "scoped css bundles do not have matching endpoints"
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

Since 11.0.100-rc.2, a Debug build of a `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` project fails when it has a `ProjectReference` to another `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` project with `OutputType=Library`. Neither project has a `wwwroot`, Razor components or other static web assets of its own.

The asset in the error is the dotnet-watch browser-tools JS initializer added in #56118 (backported to release/11.0.1xx in #56362). As far as I can tell, each referenced Web SDK project contributes its own build-only initializer as a `JSModule`/`JSLibraryModule` asset. The consuming project's `GenerateJSModuleManifestBuildStaticWebAssets` then finds no endpoint for it. The error shows up once per referenced Web SDK project.

### Steps to reproduce

Full repro: https://gist.github.com/Tragetaschen/94386201172001758266a244b371a745

Equivalent steps:
```
dotnet new web -o App
dotnet new web -o Lib
```
- In `Lib/Lib.csproj`, set `<OutputType>Library</OutputType>` and delete `Lib/Program.cs`.
- Add the reference: `dotnet add App reference Lib/Lib.csproj`.

```
dotnet build App -c Debug
```

### Expected behavior

The build succeeds, as it does with 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128 and .NET 10

### Actual behavior

```
...\Sdks\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets\targets\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.JSModules.targets(233,3): error : The following scoped css bundles do not have matching endpoints: _framework/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BlazorWeb.DotNetWatch#[.{fingerprint}]!.lib.module.js [...\App\App.csproj]
```

### Is this a regression?

yes

| SDK / configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, Debug | fails |
| 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, Release | builds |
| 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, Debug, `EnableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile=false` in Lib | builds |
| 11.0.100-rc.1.26425.128, Debug | builds |


### Are there any workarounds?

Set `<EnableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile>false</EnableHotReloadInRuntimeConfigDevFile>` in the referenced library project.

Issues.Title: Preserve source locations when replaying restore diagnostics
Issues.Body:
Fixes: https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_workitems/edit/2905535 as part of the coordinated Visual Studio navigation fix.

Preserve diagnostic files and coordinates through the SDK assets cache and MSBuild logging. Rebind supported diagnostics to current, uniquely identified PackageReference declarations so navigation remains correct when they move during a no-op restore. This is needed here because ResolvePackageAssets drops NuGet locations before Visual Studio displays the warning. Missing or ambiguous origins keep the project fallback; source-only moves do not rewrite restore files or invalidate the assets cache.

Merge 4 of 4. Recommended integration order is MSBuild → NuGet.Client → project-system → SDK, not a strict compile-dependency chain. The full Visual Studio fix needs all four changes to ship.

Companion PRs, in order:
1. [dotnet/msbuild#14731](https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/pull/14731)
2. [NuGet/NuGet.Client#7766](https://github.com/NuGet/NuGet.Client/pull/7766)
3. [dotnet-project-system PR 794612 (Azure DevOps)](https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_git/dotnet-project-system/pullrequest/794612)
4. [dotnet/sdk#56655](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/56655) — **this PR**

Issues.Title: Restore validation, cleanup, and tool shims for optimized Native AOT publish
Issues.Body:
🤖 Restore three build contracts skipped by optimized Native AOT publishing, in three separate commits.

## Changes

- Run `_CheckForInvalidConfigurationAndPlatform` before the optimized build prerequisites, restoring hooked SDK validations such as the runtime identifier/platform mismatch diagnostic (`NETSDK1032`).
- Wrap optimized build prerequisites and SDK extensions in `_BuildForOptimizedPublish`, run `IncrementalClean` before publish post-processing, and use `_CleanRecordFileWrites` on build failure. This restores intermediate DLL/PDB/XML/generated-file cleanup and removes obsolete tracked managed outputs after a prior full build without restoring managed build copies. This does not add cleanup tracking for every native or publish artifact.
- Extend the optimized build pipeline from PackTool with `GenerateShimsAssets` only when explicit tool shim runtime identifiers are requested, before cleanup and publish file collection. Preserve existing full-build and `NoBuild` shim behavior.

Each commit includes regression coverage and updates to `documentation/general/publish-build-optimization.md`.

## Validation

- Built the SDK redist, refreshed it after the target changes, and verified the deployed Publish/PackTool target hashes match the source.
- Passed 15 focused `Microsoft.NET.Publish.Tests` cases: platform validation, successful and repeated publish cleanup, prior full build followed by optimized publish, failure before/after compilation followed by clean, optimized/full/no-build tool shims, no requested shims, managed tool shim compatibility, optimized output layout, the CoreBuild dependency guard, and unsupported optimized publish modes.
- Passed 7 `Microsoft.NET.ILLink.Tests` smoke cases selected from the configured ILLink scope.
- Independently reproduced all three regressions using unchanged target overlays with the installed 11.0 RC1 SDK, then verified the fixes using real Native AOT compilation and retained per-invocation binlogs.
- Targeted test TRX files and build binlogs are retained under `artifacts/log/targeted-tests/`. Validation was on Windows x64; Linux/macOS were not run locally. The full SDK build succeeded with existing NU1902/NU1903 audit warnings for `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` 8.0.1 in ApiCompat projects; those dependencies were not changed or suppressed by this PR.

## Scope and related fixes

Targets `release/11.0.1xx` from its provisioned baseline. This PR neither modifies nor includes the XML documentation repair in #56620 (for #56618), or the build-hook ordering repair in #56649 (for #56645). XML cleanup coverage disables publishing documentation so it tests compiler-output tracking independently of #56620. `NoBuild` remains a separate publish path.

Issues.Title: Restore Build target ordering for optimized AOT publish
Issues.Body:
Optimized AOT publish ran `PrepareResources` before `ResolveReferences`, so resources added by `BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences"` hooks were omitted from compilation. The optimized target chain now preserves the relevant `CoreBuildDependsOn` ordering.

- **Target ordering:** Run `PreBuildEvent` and `ResolveReferences` before `PrepareResources`, then `ResolveKeySource` before `Compile`.
- **Regression coverage:** Assert the optimized AOT publish target sequence.

For example, targets that contribute resources through this hook run before resource preparation:

```xml
<Target Name="AddResources" BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences">
  <ItemGroup>
    <EmbeddedResource Include="Resources/*.resx" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Target>
```

- Fixes #56645

Issues.Title: Static web assets from a NuGet package are not compressed on their fingerprinted route (project references are)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

When a Razor class library is consumed as a **NuGet package**, its static web assets get compressed (`.gz` / `.br`) endpoints only on their plain route. The fingerprinted route, which is what `@Assets["..."]` returns, has no `Content-Encoding` selectors, so `MapStaticAssets` always serves it uncompressed.

The same library consumed as a **project reference** gets both compressed variants on the fingerprinted route, as expected.

So with a package reference, following the template guidance (`@Assets[...]` + `MapStaticAssets`) for a library stylesheet makes it larger on the wire than linking it by its plain path. In our app, a 429 KB library stylesheet went out raw under its fingerprinted name and as 63 KB of Brotli under its plain name.

The SDK-generated `@import` of a package's `<Lib>.<fp>.bundle.scp.css` in the app's scoped CSS bundle is affected in the same way, and an app cannot work around that one.

This may share a root cause with #54907.

### To reproduce (SDK 10.0.100, Linux)

```bash
dotnet new razorclasslib -n DemoLib -o DemoLib
mkdir -p DemoLib/wwwroot/css
python3 -c "print('.demo{color:red}\n'*4000)" > DemoLib/wwwroot/css/demo.css
dotnet pack DemoLib -c Release -o feed -p:Version=1.0.0

dotnet new blazor -n DemoApp -o DemoApp --interactivity Server --empty
# nuget.config in DemoApp pointing at ./feed, then:
dotnet add DemoApp package DemoLib --version 1.0.0
dotnet publish DemoApp -c Release -o pub
```

Then list the endpoints for `demo` in `pub/DemoApp.staticwebassets.endpoints.json` (Route | AssetFile | Content-Encoding selector).

**Package reference:**

```
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.0q6p3fhpob.css | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css     | []
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.css            | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css     | []
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.css            | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.gz  | ['gzip']
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.css            | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.br  | ['br']
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.br         | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.br  | []
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.gz         | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.gz  | []
```

**Project reference** (`dotnet add DemoApp reference DemoLib/DemoLib.csproj` instead):

```
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.0q6p3fhpob.css    | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.gz | ['gzip']
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.0q6p3fhpob.css    | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.br | ['br']
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.0q6p3fhpob.css    | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css    | []
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.0q6p3fhpob.css.br | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.br | []
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.0q6p3fhpob.css.gz | _content/DemoLib/css/demo.css.gz | []
_content/DemoLib/css/demo.css               | ... (same as above, plain route)
```

### Expected behavior

A package asset's fingerprinted route gets the same `gzip` / `br` endpoints as a project-reference asset, so `@Assets[...]` and the scoped bundle `@import` are served compressed.

### Notes

This looks like it's because a package asset's relative path carries no `#[.{fingerprint}]` pattern, so the compressed asset's path (`css/demo.css.gz`) never produces a fingerprinted compressed endpoint for compression negotiation to attach to. None of the switches in `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Compression.targets` change this; they only choose which assets and formats are compressed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Static web assets from a NuGet package are not compressed on their fingerprinted route (project references are)" (#56648)

Issues.Title: Optimized AOT publish (#54515) leaves out ResolveReferences before PrepareResources, so BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences" resource targets are skipped
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

Since #54515 (milestone `11.0-rc2`), `UseOptimizedPublish` defaults to true for `PublishAot`, and `Publish` runs `_BeforeOptimizedPublishTargets` instead of `Build`:

```
BuildOnlySettings; PrepareForBuild; PrepareResources; Compile; CreateSatelliteAssemblies
```

`CoreBuildDependsOn` in `Microsoft.Common.CurrentVersion.targets` is different:

```
BuildOnlySettings; PrepareForBuild; PreBuildEvent; ResolveReferences; PrepareResources; ResolveKeySource; Compile; ...
```

The optimized list leaves out `PreBuildEvent`, `ResolveReferences` and `ResolveKeySource`. In particular `ResolveReferences` no longer runs **before** `PrepareResources`. It only runs later, pulled in by `Compile`. Anything that is hooked to run `BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences"` and adds `EmbeddedResource` (or other resource) items now adds them after `AssignTargetPaths` and `CreateManifestResourceNames` have already run. The items are never passed to the compiler, and nothing reports it.

This broke Avalonia's XAML in a Native AOT app of mine. `AddAvaloniaResources` in [`AvaloniaBuildTasks.targets`](https://github.com/AvaloniaUI/Avalonia/blob/master/packages/Avalonia/AvaloniaBuildTasks.targets) is declared `BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences"` and adds the `!AvaloniaResources` `EmbeddedResource`. The published app crashes at startup with `XamlLoadException: No precompiled XAML found for ...` (reported to Avalonia as AvaloniaUI/Avalonia#22465). Any other package or build extension that contributes embedded resources the same way will hit the same thing.

Target order from a binary log of the same project, same SDK:

- `dotnet build`: `AddAvaloniaResources` → `ResolveReferences` → `AssignTargetPaths` → `CreateManifestResourceNames` → `GenerateAvaloniaResources` → `CoreResGen` → `PrepareResources` → `CoreCompile`.
- `dotnet publish` with `PublishAot`: `AssignTargetPaths` → `CreateManifestResourceNames` first, and only later `AddAvaloniaResources` → `ResolveReferences` → `GenerateAvaloniaResources` → `CoreResGen` → `PrepareResources` → `CoreCompile`. The `Csc` command line has a single `/resource:` argument and no `!AvaloniaResources`.

This looks like the same family as #56618 (a `Build`-path behaviour that the optimized path no longer provides).

### Steps to reproduce

I reproduced it in a real app, not a minimal sample. The shape of a minimal repro:

1. .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, a project with `<PublishAot>true</PublishAot>`.
2. Add a target that adds an `EmbeddedResource` the way many packages do:

   ```xml
   <Target Name="AddGeneratedResource" BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences">
     <ItemGroup>
       <EmbeddedResource Include="$(IntermediateOutputPath)generated.bin" LogicalName="!Generated" />
     </ItemGroup>
   </Target>
   ```

3. `dotnet publish -c Release -r linux-x64`, then check the intermediate assembly's manifest resources. With `-p:UseOptimizedPublish=false` the resource is present; with the default it is missing.

I have not run this exact snippet, so please treat the steps as a sketch. The Avalonia case is the verified one.

### Expected behavior

Publishing with `PublishAot` gives the same compile inputs as `Build`. Targets that hook into the `Build` path with `BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences"` still take effect.

### Actual behavior

Such targets run too late to matter, with no warning. In my app the failure only appears at run time.

### Known workarounds

`<UseOptimizedPublish>false</UseOptimizedPublish>` restores the full `Build`, as the comment in `Microsoft.NET.Publish.targets` says. With it, the same app starts normally.

### Suggestions

- Add `ResolveReferences` (and probably `PreBuildEvent` and `ResolveKeySource`) to `_BeforeOptimizedPublishTargets`, in the same positions as `CoreBuildDependsOn`, so extensions that hook those targets behave as they do in `Build`.
- Or document the omitted targets as a breaking change. The `11.0 RC2` SDK release notes do not mention the new default, and `_AdditionalOptimizedPublishTargets` runs after `Compile`, which is too late for resource-contributing targets.

### Configuration

- SDK: 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105
- OS: Linux (Fedora), x64
- `PublishAot` true, Avalonia 12.1.4

### Other information

Related: #54515 (the change), #56618 (a different breakage from the same change), #56484 and #55911 (plans to widen the optimized publish).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Optimized AOT publish (#54515) leaves out ResolveReferences before PrepareResources, so BeforeTargets="ResolveReferences" resource targets are skipped" (#56645)

Issues.Title: Fix dotnet watch shutdown with connected browser tools
Issues.Body:
Fixes #56584.

Browser-tools WebSocket forwarding only observed `RequestAborted`. Kestrel waits for upgraded requests during graceful shutdown before aborting them, so connected browsers could keep the application alive beyond watch's five-second cleanup deadline, leading to a forced kill and exit code `-1`.

Link both forwarding pumps to `IHostApplicationLifetime.ApplicationStopping` and handle expected shutdown cancellation without logging an application error. HTTP forwarding, provider handshakes, and non-shutdown failure handling remain unchanged.

Adds a regression test with one and two open browser connections through real Kestrel and production hosting-startup wiring. It checks that application shutdown completes within five seconds and all provider connections terminate before browser cleanup.

**Validation:** Both regression rows failed with shutdown timeouts before the fix. The final browser-refresh suite passed all 17 tests across 10 runs (170 executions), with zero build warnings or errors. Tests directly reference the rebuilt middleware; executed with `scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Watch.BrowserRefresh.Tests\Microsoft.AspNetCore.Watch.BrowserRefresh.Tests.csproj --repeat 10 --skip-redist-check`.

**Limitation:** The exact shipped .NET 11 `dotnet watch` Ctrl+C scenario was not validated end to end.

Issues.Title: Native companion asset declaration and transitive content flow for file-based C# apps ('#:ref')
Issues.Body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

We are building modular file-based C# applications in .NET 11, where an entry-point program (`app.cs`) references a file-based library (`lib.cs`) using `#:ref`. The library needs to carry companion content files (such as `template.json`, configuration defaults, or static data) that should be copied to the application's runtime base directory (`AppContext.BaseDirectory`).

However, this is currently impossible through native file-based directives:
1. `#:include` maps `.json` to `<None>` with `CopyToOutputDirectory=Never`.
2. `#:include` does not accept trailing MSBuild metadata (e.g., `#:include data.json CopyToOutputDirectory=PreserveNewest` fails because the parser interprets the metadata as part of the file name).
3. `#:property` only populates `<PropertyGroup>`, so it cannot declare MSBuild Items like `<Content>` or `<EmbeddedResource>`.
4. In `dotnet run`, compilation occurs in isolated `%TEMP%` directories. Assets residing alongside a referenced library are not automatically copied to the caller's execution directory unless the caller explicitly creates MSBuild `.targets` files and writes `<Import Project="..." />` with `$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)`.

The moment a file-based program needs to carry a companion physical file, the "zero-config, single-file" experience breaks down, forcing developers back into manual MSBuild XML authoring.

### Describe the solution you'd like

We would like to see first-class, directive-driven asset declaration and transitive content distribution for file-based apps:

#### 1. Directive-level Asset Declaration
Support declaring content or resource assets directly via file-level directives:
```csharp
// Option A: Dedicated directives for items
#:content template.json
#:resource logo.png

// Option B: Allow trailing MSBuild item metadata on #:include
#:include template.json CopyToOutputDirectory=PreserveNewest
```

#### 2. Transitive Content Flow Across `#:ref`
When `app.cs` references `lib.cs` via `#:ref`:
- The virtual project generated for `lib.cs` should expose its declared content items via standard MSBuild items (`ContentWithTargetPath`).
- MSBuild's native `GetCopyToOutputDirectoryItems` target should automatically flow these assets into the consumer's execution directory in both `dotnet run` (temp bin cache) and `dotnet publish` (release output), identical to how NuGet `contentFiles` or traditional `ProjectReference` content behaves.

### Alternatives you've considered

1. **Forcing all assets into `EmbeddedResource`**:
   While `EmbeddedResource` works well for immutable data, it cannot support scenarios where files must exist on disk for user/operator editing after deployment (e.g., editable configuration files or user-customizable templates).
2. **Manual `Directory.Build.targets` with `<Import Project="..." />`**:
   Requires both the consumer and library to maintain custom MSBuild XML files with `Link` mappings. This couples the consumer to the library's physical directory structure and reintroduces MSBuild complexity.
3. **External wrapper / copy scripts**:
   Using external scripts (PowerShell / bash) to move files prior to execution breaks the native `dotnet run <file.cs>` workflow.

### Additional context

One of the primary value propositions of file-based C# is to compete with script-friendly ecosystems (Python, Node.js), where companion asset files naturally reside alongside scripts without complex build system ceremony. Enabling seamless companion asset distribution would make file-based C# truly self-contained for real-world automation, CLI tools, and modular utilities.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Native companion asset declaration and transitive content flow for file-based C# apps ('#:ref')" (#56642)

Issues.Title: Unify dependency referencing under '#:include' with optional call-site isolation ('As=Library')
Issues.Body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

We are working with file-based C# applications in .NET 11 and trying to progressively modularize our codebases, but we encounter two distinct friction points with the current triad of dependency directives (`#:include`, `#:ref`, and `#:project`):

1. **Refactoring friction during code evolution**:
   A `.cs` file often starts as a shared source slice (`#:include Helper.cs`). When it matures into an independent file-based library (`#:property OutputType=Library`), all consumer files must be manually rewritten from `#:include` to `#:ref` (and vice versa). The internal packaging decision of a dependency leaks to every call site.
2. **Directive conflicts in multi-file composition ([#54090](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/54090))**:
   When composing multiple source files, directive collisions (e.g., Nullable context, C# language versions, package versions) can occur. Callers currently have no way to isolate a conflicting dependency into its own compilation sandbox at the call site unless the dependency file itself is modified.

### Describe the solution you'd like

We would like to explore unifying external dependency intake under a single, intuitive `#:include` directive, complemented by an optional modifier for explicit compilation boundaries:

```csharp
#:include <Path> [As=Library|Source]
```

#### 1. Conventional Defaults (when `As` is omitted)
The SDK resolves dependencies deterministically by the target's physical shape and metadata:
- **Project Directory (`path/`) or `*.csproj`**: Resolved as a traditional `ProjectReference` (looks for `.csproj` in the directory, matching `dotnet build <dir>`).
- **Wildcard (`*.cs`, `**/*.cs`)**: Resolved as source inclusion (`@(Compile)`).
- **Single `.cs` declaring `OutputType=Library`**: Built in an isolated virtual project and referenced (`ProjectReference`).
- **Single `.cs` (plain)**: Resolved as source inclusion (`@(Compile)`).
- **Assembly (`*.dll`)**: Resolved as an assembly reference (`@(Reference)`).

#### 2. Explicit Call-Site Override (`As=Library | Source`)
Callers can explicitly assert an isolated compilation boundary:
```csharp
#:include ../Common/LegacyHelper.cs As=Library
```
- Specifying `As=Library` instructs the SDK to build the target within an isolated virtual compilation context, linking the resulting assembly to the host application.
- This provides callers with an explicit, opt-in escape hatch to isolate directive conflicts locally without modifying upstream files.

### Alternatives you've considered

1. **Keeping the status quo (`#:include`, `#:ref`, `#:project`)**:
   Maintains a direct 1:1 mapping with internal MSBuild concepts (`Compile`, `ProjectReference`), but imposes cognitive overhead on developers to track whether a target is a `.csproj`, an independent file-based library, or a code slice.
2. **Only merging `#:ref` and `#:project`**:
   Unifies `.cs` and `.csproj` project references, but leaves the transition gap between source inclusion and library references unaddressed.
3. **Automatic compiler isolation on conflict**:
   Having the compiler automatically isolate files when directive collisions are detected. However, implicit isolation may unexpectedly break `partial` classes or `internal` accessibility; an explicit `As=Library` modifier at the call site is more predictable and transparent.

### Additional context

This proposal is directly complementary to the multi-file directive collision discussions in [#54090](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/54090). Providing callers with an opt-in `As=Library` switch empowers consumers to resolve collisions locally without requiring complex global merge rules or breaking changes to upstream dependencies.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "Unify dependency referencing under '#:include' with optional call-site isolation ('As=Library')" (#56641)

Issues.Title: Escaping more quotation marks in PowerShell help descriptions.
Issues.Body:
Reopen #55040. The fix is still relevant and I'd like to see it land in the .NET 11 in next month if possible. Thanks!

Currently, the `SanitizeHelpDescription` function does not escape curly quotes `“` and `”`. However, PowerShell utilizes "smart quotes", which causes it to mistakenly interpret curly quotes within Simplified Chinese command descriptions as string delimiters, breaking the PowerShell completions script.

This PR adds escaping for `“` and `”` to resolve the PowerShell string delimiting issue. Additionally, it escapes `„`, which should help prevent similar issues with PowerShell completion in languages like German.

Since we surround command descriptions with double quotes (`"`), escaping single quotes (`'`) should be unnecessary.

Fix: #51260
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Escaping more quotation marks in PowerShell help descriptions." (#56640)

Issues.Title: CA2000 false positive when a disposable is passed to a primary constructor and stored
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

If a disposable is passed to a primary constructor that stores it, CA2000 reports a leak where the disposable is created. That's true whether it's stored through a property initializer, a field initializer or a captured parameter. The same code with an explicit constructor reports nothing. This looks like the CA2000 counterpart of dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#7803 (CA2213): the analyzer doesn't see the primary constructor's initializers when it follows the call into the constructor.

### Steps to reproduce

.editorconfig: `dotnet_diagnostic.CA2000.severity = warning`

```csharp
public sealed class Res : IDisposable { public void Dispose() { } }

public sealed class Explicit
{
    public Explicit(Res r) { R = r; }
    public Res R { get; }
}

public sealed class PrimaryProperty(Res r) { public Res R { get; } = r; }
public sealed class PrimaryField(Res r) { private readonly Res _r = r; public Res R => _r; }
public sealed class PrimaryCaptured(Res r) { public Res R => r; }

public static class Use
{
    public static Explicit A() => new(new Res());        // no diagnostic
    public static PrimaryProperty B() => new(new Res()); // CA2000
    public static PrimaryField C() => new(new Res());    // CA2000
    public static PrimaryCaptured D() => new(new Res()); // CA2000
}
```

### Expected behavior

None of the four call sites gets a diagnostic. In each case the object is handed to the new instance, which stores it.

### Actual behavior

B, C and D report CA2000: Call `System.IDisposable.Dispose` on object created by 'new Res()' before all references to it are out of scope. A doesn't.

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

Use an explicit constructor, or suppress CA2000 at the call site.
